subject: Benchmarking plan & witness testing schedule for NovaFS RFP
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
To: Simon Clarke <simon.clarke@novafs.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Benchmarking plan & witness testing schedule for NovaFS RFP

Simon —

Thanks for the RFP follow-up. Per the procurement timeline you shared, we drafted a targeted benchmarking plan that covers latency/throughput at target concurrency, scaling behavior during step-load, and deterministic tail-latency characterization. Attached is a concise plan and the proposed test matrix (redwood_perf_plan_v1.pdf, novafs_test_matrix.xlsx).

Key highlights:
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency per model size, sustained tokens/sec at fixed batch sizes, cold-start times, cache hit/miss rates.
- Workloads: 3 representative profile mixes (low-latency interactive, bursty medium-concurrency, and high-throughput batch inference).
- Fixtures: controlled synthetic client (JMeter + custom token generator) + replay of the anonymized snippet workload you shared.
- Scaling: vertical concurrency sweep then horizontal scaling (add nodes) to observe saturation and per-node efficiency.

We recommend an on-site or virtual witness window the week of 26 Jan — we can run the witness replay and share raw and aggregated CSVs. Please confirm: 1) desired models (open-model names or sizes), 2) whether the witness needs VPN access or will use screen-share only, and 3) any compliance observer you need listed on the access log.

Next steps: if you confirm the witness window we’ll lock test bed specs and share the pre-test checklist (network ACLs, test accounts).

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_perf_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: novafs_test_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)]

From: Simon Clarke <simon.clarke@novafs.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@procure.novafs.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Benchmarking plan & witness testing schedule for NovaFS RFP

Olga —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the plan. A few clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Models: please include one 7B and one 34B config (quantized where supported). We plan to compare cost/latency tradeoffs.
2) Data handling: will Redwood run tests on hosted infra or on a dedicated VPC? Our security team requires an audit log of any access during witness.
3) Success criteria: our procurement lead wants p95 < 350ms for the interactive profile at 40 concurrent users for the 7B model; and cost-per-1M tokens numbers for both configs.

Also, can you share a short statement on how you handle prefix caching and whether caching would be enabled during witness runs?

Simon
Head of Platform Engineering
Nova Financial Systems

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.example>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Benchmarking plan & witness testing schedule for NovaFS RFP

Simon, Priya, Olga —

Short answers to the technical points:

1) Test bed: we propose running the formal benchmark on Redwood Dedicated in a customer-dedicated VPC image (same isolation model we use for Dedicated trials). That gives reproducible network characteristics and full audit logging. We can, alternatively, run on hosted infra if you prefer that path.

2) Models and quantization: we’ll provision a 7B fp16 and a 34B 4-bit quantized variant. For fairness we will keep batch sizes consistent across runs and report both raw and normalized tokens/sec.

3) Caching: by default prefix/KV caching is OFF for the baseline runs. We will then enable caching as a second pass to measure improvement and cache hit/miss distributions. We will label all results accordingly.

4) Metrics & instrumentation: per-request timing includes client send, gateway, runtime queuing, model token emission, and end-to-end observed latency. We’ll provide p50/p90/p95/p99 and throughput curves. Kernel-level telemetry and GPU utilisation traces are available on request during witness windows.

5) p95 target: we will run a focused saturation sweep to determine whether the 7B config meets p95 < 350ms at 40 concurrent interactive clients; we’ll tune batching and concurrency to illustrate operational tradeoffs.

Attachment: initial run script and environment spec attached for review (see novafs_test_matrix.xlsx).

—Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
[Inline: quoted previous messages]

From: Marcus Ellis <marcus.ellis@benchlabs.io>

Date: Tue, 27 Jan 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Benchmarking plan & witness testing schedule for NovaFS RFP

Hi all —

BenchLabs will act as the independent witness for NovaFS. We can observe the runs remotely and collect our own metrics. A couple of asks from our side before we watch:

• Please provide read-only access credentials to the test metrics dashboard (Grafana endpoint) for the witness window.
• Share the exact workload replay file and seed list so we can validate determinism.
• Confirm whether any autoscaling policies will be enabled during the witness run (we prefer a fixed-capacity run for the initial baseline, then a second run with autoscale enabled).

If Redwood can deliver the raw CSVs after the run, we’ll run an independent post-analysis and deliver a short witness report. Proposed witness window: 27 Jan 13:00 - 17:00 PST; we’ll be on Zoom.

Thanks,
Marcus Ellis
Lead Test Engineer, BenchLabs

Simon/Priya/Marcus —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Confirming logistics and actions below:

1) Witness window: 27 Jan 13:00 - 17:00 PST accepted by BenchLabs; Redwood will provide the Grafana dashboard and a Zoom link.

2) Access & audit: we will provision read-only Grafana tokens and a short-lived SSH jump for audit purposes (all access logged to the tenant audit trail). We will send the access bundle 24 hours prior to the window.

3) Test profile: baseline (no prefix caching, fixed capacity), then caching-enabled run, then autoscale-enabled run. We will label results: baseline/with-caching/with-autoscale.

4) Success criteria capture: we will run the saturation sweep for the 7B config and produce a run that shows p95 numbers alongside throughput and cost estimates. Expect a summary CSV within 24 hours of the window (redwood_test_results_20260127.csv).

5) Deliverables: aggregated latency percentiles, tokens/sec curves, GPU utilization traces (sampled), kernel time breakdowns, and the raw CSVs. We will also provide a short technical note on how caching changed effective request latency and token throughput.

Next steps for procurement: Priya, please confirm whether NovaFS requires an NDA addendum for BenchLabs to access witness artifacts; if so we’ll route DocuSign.

Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
